numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Taking positions from a SparseArray with allow_fill=True promotes the result subtype based on the type of the fill value (np.result_type(dtype, type(fill_value))) whenever a taken position lands on a gap or a -1 index, even for an identity take such as arr.take([0, 1, 2], allow_fill=True). Examples: Sparse[int8, 0] becomes Sparse[int64, 0]; Sparse[uint64, 0] becomes Sparse[float64, 0] and rounds values above 2**53; Sparse[datetime64[ns], Timestamp(...)] becomes Sparse[object] holding raw integers; Sparse[datetime64[s], Timestamp(...)] becomes Sparse[datetime64[us]]; Sparse[datetime64[ns]] with no gaps raises DTypePromotionError.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The dtype should be preserved for gaps, since SparseDtype._check_fill_value already guarantees a non-NA fill value fits the subtype; for a -1 index the promotion should follow the value rather than its type. An identity take should round-trip without changing the subtype.
trigger_conditions: SparseArray.take called with allow_fill=True on an identity index list such as [0, 1, 2]
a taken position lands on a gap (sparse fill position) or on a -1 index
subtype is int8, uint64, datetime64[ns] with NaT or Timestamp fill, datetime64[s] with Timestamp fill, or datetime64[ns] with no gaps
reached in practice via Series.reindex, DataFrame.reindex, .loc[list], alignment and GroupBy.first/last

oracle_clues: PR body states the identity take arr.take([0, 1, 2], allow_fill=True) should round-trip
commit notes the fix must avoid a unitless NaT so the datetimelike fill uses the subtype's own unit
the fix replaces np.result_type promotions with a _promote_for_fill helper that keeps dtype when can_hold_element holds the value and defers to maybe_promote otherwise

numerical_characteristics.dtype: Sparse[int8, 0], Sparse[uint64, 0], Sparse[datetime64[ns]] and Sparse[datetime64[s]] with Timestamp or NaT fill
numerical_characteristics.precision: uint64 values above 2**53 lose precision when promoted to float64 (Sparse[uint64, 0] becomes Sparse[float64, 0]); datetime64[s] is widened to datetime64[us]; datetime64[ns] is widened via maybe_promote; NaT fill must use the subtype's own unit, since a unitless NaT is deprecated in numpy 2.5
category_specific_evidence: SparseArray._take_with_fill chose its result dtype via np.result_type(dtype, type(fill_value)) whenever a taken position landed on a gap or a -1 index, so arr.take([0, 1, 2], allow_fill=True) did not round-trip.
Sparse[uint64, 0] became Sparse[float64, 0], rounding values above 2**53.
Sparse[datetime64[ns], Timestamp] became Sparse[object] holding raw integers.
Sparse[datetime64[ns]] with no gaps raised DTypePromotionError.

The fix adds a _promote_for_fill helper: it keeps the dtype when can_hold_element holds the value and defers to maybe_promote otherwise, because maybe_promote's datetime64 arm widens to M8[ns] when the fill unit differs.
A Timestamp/Timedelta fill is unboxed to asm8 because np.full would truncate it to microseconds.
The added test asserts result.dtype.subtype == np.dtype(unit) and result[3] is pd.NaT for take with allow_fill=True.
The defect dates to the ExtensionArray refactor in commit 56d8e789155 (2018); related issues GH-65478 and GH-49631 are cited.
reproduction_risks: The passages do not state a tolerance at which correct and incorrect answers separate, nor any 1-ULP or default-tolerance behaviour; tolerance is left null.
Identity take with allow_fill=True must preserve the subtype; a unitless NaT fill is deprecated in numpy 2.5 (commit note only, not a pinned requirement).
Using maybe_promote alone would widen datetime64[s] to [ns].
Reproducing the uint64 precision loss requires values above 2**53; the passages do not give a specific example value.

provenance.value: Taking positions from a SparseArray with allow_fill=True promotes the result subtype based on the type of the fill value (np.result_type(dtype, type(fill_value))) whenever a taken position lands on a gap or a -1 index, even for an identity take such as arr.take([0, 1, 2], allow_fill=True). Examples: Sparse[int8, 0] becomes Sparse[int64, 0]; Sparse[uint64, 0] becomes Sparse[float64, 0] and rounds values above 2**53; Sparse[datetime64[ns], Timestamp(...)] becomes Sparse[object] holding raw integers; Sparse[datetime64[s], Timestamp(...)] becomes Sparse[datetime64[us]]; Sparse[datetime64[ns]] with no gaps raises DTypePromotionError.

The dtype should be preserved for gaps, since SparseDtype._check_fill_value already guarantees a non-NA fill value fits the subtype; for a -1 index the promotion should follow the value rather than its type. An identity take should round-trip without changing the subtype.
